wu2026chainmpq: Relation hallucinations are the most common yet least studied failure of LVLMs. ChainMPQ is training-free: it extracts subject and object keywords from the question to highlight image regions, then asks multi-perspective questions about the subject, object, and linking relation in sequence, carrying textual and visual memory from earlier steps into later ones. The interleaved image-text chain builds up relational inference progressively. Across LVLMs and benchmarks it sharply reduces relation hallucination, with ablations confirming each of the three components.
xie2026hierarchical: Concept bottleneck models classify through human-understandable concepts, but at a single semantic level, unlike humans who reason at multiple abstraction levels. HIL-CBM adds hierarchy without relational concept annotations: a gradient-based visual consistency loss pushes abstraction layers to attend to similar spatial regions, and dual classification heads operate on concepts at different abstraction levels, aligning explanation granularity with predictions from abstract to concrete. It beats sparse CBMs on accuracy and, per human evaluation, gives more interpretable, accurate explanations while staying label-free.
xiong2025map: Reasoning LLMs produce long chain-of-thought but behave unstably, degrading under few-shot prompting in counterintuitive ways. A graph framework clusters verbose CoT into semantically coherent steps and builds directed reasoning graphs that capture dependencies among steps. Across models and prompting regimes, structural features such as exploration density, branching, and convergence correlate strongly with accuracy, and prompting substantially reshapes the internal reasoning graph. The framework offers a way to evaluate reasoning quality beyond final answers and to guide prompt engineering.
xiong2026diffusionllm: Autoregressive LLMs still struggle to emit reliable structured output such as JSON, which matters for function calling. Diffusion LLMs share global information across positions and reverse the generation order, properties S3 exploits: it seeds a schema template directly in the output context as the denoising starting state instead of relying on prompt engineering. The framework improves structure adherence, content fidelity, and faithfulness of generated JSON, showing that diffusion architectures are well suited to controllable generation.
xu2025how: Documents often carry watermarks, and an evaluation across document types, watermark positions, and contents finds watermarks can cut VLM document-understanding accuracy by up to 36 percent. Scattered watermarks disturb more than centered ones, and semantically meaningful watermarks disrupt more than simple occlusion. Attention and embedding analyses trace the drop to widespread attention redistribution and shifted semantic representations, motivating robust inference on watermarked documents in finance, law, and academia.
yang2024alignedcotpromptinglargelanguage: Handcrafted few-shot demonstrations mismatch how LLMs think, and prompting style is fragile. AlignedCoT probes, refines, and formats the model's own chain of thought iteratively to produce step-wise demonstrations the model is aligned with, working zero-shot without human-crafted examples. On math and commonsense reasoning it beats human-designed demonstrations, and rewriting GSM8K into the aligned style yields a GSM8K-Align dataset that also helps retrieval-augmented generation.
yang2025optibench: Optimization benchmarks test only linear programming, far from real applied optimization. OptiBench covers end-to-end problems, linear and nonlinear, with and without tabular data, requiring models to call code solvers for exact numeric answers. To combat data scarcity, ReSocratic synthesizes optimization demonstrations by first building formal math step by step and then back-translating them into natural-language questions, producing the ReSocratic-29K dataset. Supervised fine-tuning on it closes much of the gap between small open-source models and closed models on optimization modeling.
yang2026accordion: Long chain-of-thought grows KV cache linearly and attention quadratically. Accordion-Thinking trains the model to self-regulate step granularity: a Fold mode periodically summarizes reasoning and discards earlier thoughts, reducing history-token dependence, while reinforcement learning rewards the compression. Over training, the accuracy gap between Fold and exhaustive Unfold narrows to zero, showing the model packs essentials into summaries. On a 48GB GPU it triples throughput without accuracy loss, and the step summaries double as a human-readable reasoning trace.
yang2026depthbreadth: RLVR under-explores problem difficulty and training breadth: GRPO down-weights hard, low-accuracy problems. Difficulty-Adaptive Rollout Sampling re-weights hard problems through targeted multi-stage rollouts and rebalancing schedules, improving Pass@K, while simply enlarging rollout size hurts. Scaling batch size for breadth, by contrast, raises Pass@1 through higher token entropy and less gradient noise. Combining DARS with large-batch training, DARS-Breadth, improves both Pass@K and Pass@1, showing depth and breadth are orthogonal dimensions of RLVR.
yang2026wavefrontdiffusion: Diffusion language models denoise either globally, which finalizes context prematurely, or in fixed blocks, which breaks coherent semantic units. WavefrontDiffusion expands a wavefront of active tokens outward from finalized positions at the same cost as block diffusion, following the natural flow of semantics. On reasoning and code-generation benchmarks it reaches state-of-the-art denoising quality with higher semantic fidelity, showing adaptive decoding schedules matter as much as the architecture.
yao2026multimodal: RL-aligned MLLMs can raise reward scores while degrading visual reasoning, because text-only rewards cannot verify images. A controlled study across safety VQA, chart VQA, and stress tests, varying reward design, ambiguity, scale from 2B to 32B, and RL algorithms, tracks hacking with a Newly Rewarded Failure Rate. Outcome-only rewards cause up to 48.1 percent reward hacking, RL creates new failures rather than inheriting them, scaling helps but does not fix it, and GRPO is most robust while RLOO is most vulnerable. Reliable visual-evidence verifiers, not keyword checks, reduce hacking.
yao2026notsync: Audio-language models can describe events but are not tested on when events occur. A first systematic study finds timestamp predictions are consistently biased earlier or later: the error is prevalent across models and datasets, grows with audio length to tens of seconds, and varies by event type and position. A Temporal Bias Index and visualization tool quantify the systematic misalignment. The result exposes a fundamental temporal-reasoning weakness and motivates temporally robust audio architectures.
